messages:
Priya N: hey team :wave: i'm Priya (new infra SWE). following the kube-onboard doc but my kubectl only shows 'docker-desktop' and no redwood contexts after i merged kubeconfigs. when i try `kubectl -n redwood-dev get pods` i get 'Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden'. who do i ping for RBAC/namespace access?
Devex: welcome! quick checklist — run `kubectl config view --merge --flatten` then `kubectl config get-contexts`. if you see a context like `redwood-dev-west1` try `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev-west1`. also check `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n redwood-dev` to confirm RBAC. docs: https://docs.redwood.infra/onboard/kube-access
Priya N: ran `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n redwood-dev` and it returns "no". i created a serviceaccount per the doc (`onboard-priya`) and imported the kubeconfig from the console — maybe i need a RoleBinding?
Infra SRE: @Priya N i created a RoleBinding `onboard-dev-binding` in namespace `redwood-dev` binding group `devs:onboard` to the `view` role. should be live now, can you retry `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n redwood-dev`? if still blocked paste output of `kubectl config view --minify -o yaml` (mask tokens) and i'll take a look.
onboard-bot: IAM request #12345 processed by infra-scripts — rolebinding created. audit: https://internal.redwood.com/audit/12345
Priya N: ok reran — now it returns "yes" and `kubectl -n redwood-dev get pods` lists the pods. thank you!! :thumbsup: one more q: is it better to merge the SA kubeconfig into my main ~/.kube/config or keep it separate under ~/.kube/onboard/priya.kubeconfig and set KUBECONFIG when needed?
Jamison: keep it separate initially. put the SA kubeconfig in `~/.kube/onboard/priya.kubeconfig` and set `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/onboard/priya.kubeconfig` when testing. merging is fine later but easier for troubleshooting to keep separate. also check `kubectl config get-contexts -o name` to avoid surprises.
Priya N: perfect — i'll do that. thanks everyone for the fast help, closing this thread.
